chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubeyda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who died and left his wife, his sister, and his grandfather. He (peace be upon him) said: 'This is from four shares – for the wife is the quarter, and for the sister is one share, and for the grandfather are two shares'.
ai.seo_question: How is the inheritance divided between a wife, sister, and grandfather in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific shares for a wife, sister, and paternal grandfather, illustrating the application of the 'four-share' division model in Shia jurisprudence. It highlights the distinct status of the grandfather as a primary heir alongside the sister, a point of scholarly discussion regarding whether he inherits as a 'residuary' or a fixed-share heir in the presence of siblings. This ruling is foundational for understanding the hierarchy of heirs in the absence of parents or sons.
